text_block_list.name: Tamamo Cross
text_block_list.text: O flames! O gatherers! O Three Goddesses!

text_block_list.name: Inari One
text_block_list.text: Prick up your ears and behold this night!!

text_block_list.name: No Reason
text_block_list.text:
Oooh, tonight's 'Shinmeku' is truly 
magnificent! 
Such sheer ferocity—a true rite of 
horsegirls!

A day in mid-October. 
I was visiting the annual Shuntaisai with 
the Shinme horsegirls 
to scout out the festival grounds.
choice_data_list:
Make sure you don't get separated, 
everyone.
Don't wander off and get lost, okay?

text_block_list.name: Shinme
text_block_list.text:
Okaaay! 
...

text_block_list.name: Yukino Bijin
text_block_list.text:
Oh my, looks like the 'Hiki-mikoshi' has 
reached the street too!

text_block_list.name: Hiki-mikoshi Horsegirl
text_block_list.text:
Hiki-mikoshi coming through! 
Please join in with the chants, everyone!

text_block_list.name: Hiki-mikoshi Horsegirls
text_block_list.text:
Here we go, 'Heave... HO'!! 
One more time, 'Heave... HO'!!

text_block_list.name: Mayano Top Gun
text_block_list.text:
...This hiki-mikoshi doesn't cross over 
the hill, does it?

text_block_list.name: Yukino Bijin
text_block_list.text:
Fufu, the hiki-mikoshi and the 
oohiki-mikoshi are completely different! 
Even the decorations on the palanquin are 
totally distinct.

text_block_list.name: Yukino Bijin
text_block_list.text:
The chants might be the same, 
but the Oohiki is a festival native to 
Iwate.

text_block_list.name: Daiwa Scarlet
text_block_list.text:
...It looks like their yabusame follows a 
different tradition, too. 
I was taught that distributing the 
striking arrows and hit targets to humans 
was part of the custom, but...

text_block_list.name: Azuma
text_block_list.text:
In the annual Shuntaisai, we offer prayers 
to the 'Three Pillars'— 
the Three Goddesses—to wish for peace and 
tranquility.

text_block_list.name: Azuma
text_block_list.text:
However, the Goshiki Shuntaisai prays for 
the peace of horsegirls 
while also honoring the bonds shared with 
humans. 
Even with the same wish, certain 
procedures will naturally differ.

text_block_list.name: No Reason
text_block_list.text:
Still, these tasty-looking food stalls 
will be around for our festival too, 
right?

text_block_list.name: Daiwa Scarlet
text_block_list.text:
Ah, No Reason-san! 
When on earth did you buy yakisoba...?

text_block_list.name: Blast Onepiece
text_block_list.text:
Hey, hey, everyone should grab a bite too! 
They've got candy apples, grilled carrots, 
and cotton candy!

text_block_list.name: Mayano Top Gun
text_block_list.text:
Yay! 
Maya wants a candy apple!

text_block_list.name: Daiwa Scarlet
text_block_list.text:
Geez! 
We're here to scout, so everyone take this 
serious――
choice_data_list: Is there anything you want to eat?
What would you like to have?

text_block_list.name: Daiwa Scarlet
text_block_list.text: Huh? Well, but...

text_block_list.name: Azuma
text_block_list.text:
To understand a festival to the fullest, 
thoroughly enjoying it is of the utmost 
importance.

text_block_list.name: Azuma
text_block_list.text:
Come now, Lady Daiwa Scarlet. 
What shall you partake in?
choice_data_list:
Today is a festival for horsegirls, after 
all.

text_block_list.name: Daiwa Scarlet
text_block_list.text:
...I really think you spoil them way too 
much.

Tonight is the 'Shuntaisai'—a festival of 
horsegirls, 
by horsegirls, and for horsegirls.

Yet two years from now, what the Shinme 
shall perform here 
is the 'Goshiki Shuntaisai'— 
a festival honoring the sacred bond 
between humans and horsegirls.

title: The Annual Shuntaisai, the Twelve-Year Horse Festival
